key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, boosting and stabilizing the light-induced surface photovoltage while reducing grain-boundary potential barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can improve charge-carrier homogeneity and photovoltage stability in perovskite solar-cell interfaces, helping reduce performance losses.
method: Measured dark contact potential difference (CPD) and light-induced surface photovoltage (SPV)
Compared grain-boundary vs grain-interior potential dynamics under illumination
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD distribution from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from ~345 to ~417 mV, and reduced stabilization time from ~840 to ~470 s.
watch_item: The results come from thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translating these interfacial improvements into full-device durability and efficiency requires further validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
